question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Perpendicular Bisector & Equidistance)

questions.question_text: What compass radius setting is required when constructing the perpendicular bisector of segment XY?
options: B) Strictly greater than half of XY (>0.5 XY)
C) Less than half of XY
questions.correct_answer: B) Strictly greater than half of XY (>0.5 XY)

questions.question_text: Any point located on the perpendicular bisector of segment AB is:
options: A) Equidistant from endpoints A and B
B) Closer to A than B
C) At right angles to midpoint only
questions.correct_answer: A) Equidistant from endpoints A and B

questions.question_text: Which two classical instruments are exclusively permitted in geometric constructions?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An unmarked straightedge (ruler) and a pair of compasses.

questions.question_text: Is it necessary to use the same compass radius for arcs above and below segment XY when constructing its perpendicular bisector? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. Radius for top arcs can differ from bottom arcs, provided top arcs from X and Y are equal to each other (>0.5 XY) and bottom arcs from X and Y are equal to each other.

questions.question_text: Draw segment XY = 8 cm. Describe step-by-step how to construct its perpendicular bisector line AB using ruler and compass. Prove why AX = AY.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Steps: 1) Draw XY = 8 cm. 2) Set compass radius > 4 cm. Draw arcs above and below XY from X and Y meeting at A and B. 3) Join AB meeting XY at M. Proof: In ΔAMX and ΔAMY, MX = MY, ∠AMX = ∠AMY = 90°, AM = AM. By SAS, ΔAMX ≅ ΔAMY, so AX = AY by CPCT.

questions.question_text: An artist constructs a symmetrical human eye outline. The upper and lower eyelid arcs meet at corners P and Q (PQ = 6 cm). (a) What line contains the center points for both arcs? (b) Prove that any center point C on this line satisfies CP = CQ.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) The center points lie on the perpendicular bisector of segment PQ. (b) By SAS triangle congruence (ΔCMP ≅ ΔCMQ where M is midpoint of PQ), CP = CQ.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Angle Bisector & Copying Angles)

questions.question_text: Which triangle congruence criterion is applied when copying an angle using ruler and compass?
An angle bisector divides an angle of 74° into two angles measuring:
Describe step-by-step how to bisect a given angle ∠AOB.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Draw an arc from vertex O intersecting arms OA and OB at P and Q. 2) From P and Q, draw equal arcs intersecting at C. 3) Ray OC is the angle bisector.

questions.question_text: If ray OC bisects ∠AOB and ∠AOC = 28°, find the measure of ∠AOB.
Describe step-by-step how to construct a line parallel to line 'l' passing through an external point P using alternate interior angles.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Pick point A on line 'l' and draw transversal AP. 2) ∠PAL is formed. 3) At vertex P, copy ∠PAL on alternate side of transversal AP using SSS angle copy method to form ∠APM = ∠PAL. 4) Extend ray PM to form line 'm' parallel to 'l'.

questions.question_text: A carpenter wants to cut two wood panels at identical angles ∠ABC = 52°. He copies ∠ABC onto a second panel ray XY forming ∠XYZ. (a) What criterion guarantees ∠XYZ = ∠ABC? (b) If he bisects ∠XYZ with ray YW, find ∠XYW.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) SSS criterion (by copying equal arc lengths and chord distances). (b) ∠XYW = 52° / 2 = 26°.

questions.question_text: Drawing an arc on a line and intersecting it with the same compass radius from the intersection point constructs an angle of:
How is a 45° angle systematically derived using constructions?
Explain why the first arc intersection step constructs an angle of exactly 60°.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Keeping the compass radius unchanged creates an equilateral triangle with 3 equal side lengths, and every interior angle of an equilateral triangle measures 60°.

questions.question_text: Outline the construction steps to obtain a 30° angle and a 15° angle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Construct a 60° angle using equilateral arc. 2) Bisect 60° angle to get 30°. 3) Bisect 30° angle to get 15°.

questions.question_text: Describe step-by-step how to construct a 90° perpendicular angle at a given point P on line 'l' using compass and ruler.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) With center P, draw a semicircle intersecting line 'l' at A and B. 2) From A and B, draw arcs with radius > AP intersecting at C above P. 3) Draw line PC. Line PC is perpendicular to line 'l' at P (∠CPA = 90°).

questions.question_text: A solar panel installation requires mounting brackets at angles of 60°, 30°, and 45°. (a) Which basic angle is constructed first for 30°? (b) How is 45° obtained? (c) Find angle between 30° and 45° brackets.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) 60° angle is constructed first. (b) 45° is obtained by constructing 90° and bisecting it. (c) Difference = 45° - 30° = 15°.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Regular Hexagon & Architectural Patterns)

questions.question_text: How many equilateral triangles form a regular hexagon from its center point?
What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
Explain why stepping off the radius 6 times around a circle's circumference forms a regular hexagon.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Stepping off radius 'r' creates 6 adjacent chord segments of length 'r'. Each central triangle has 3 sides equal to 'r' (equilateral), subtending 6 × 60° = 360° at center.

questions.question_text: What is a pointed arch in architecture and how is it constructed geometrically?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A pointed arch consists of two circular arcs meeting at a central point at the top, constructed from center points on the base support line.

questions.question_text: Describe step-by-step how to construct a regular hexagon ABCDEF of side length 4 cm using ruler and compass.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Draw circle of radius r = 4 cm with center O. 2) Mark point A on circumference. 3) With compass set at 4 cm, draw arc from A to mark B on circle. 4) Move to B and mark C; continue stepping off points D, E, F. 5) Join AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA.

questions.question_text: An Islamic tile pattern uses a 6-pointed star rosette constructed inside a regular hexagon. (a) Find central angle of each of the 6 constituent equilateral triangles. (b) Find interior angle of hexagon. (c) Total sum of interior angles.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Central angle = 360° / 6 = 60°. (b) Interior angle = 2 × 60° = 120°. (c) Total sum = 6 × 120° = 720°.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Chapter 6 Practice Paper (Tilings & Tangram Puzzles)

questions.question_text: What two strict requirements define a valid plane tiling (tessellation)?
options: A) Zero gaps and zero overlaps
questions.correct_answer: A) Zero gaps and zero overlaps

questions.question_text: How many total pieces comprise a traditional Chinese Tangram puzzle?
List the individual shapes and quantities of the 7 Tangram pieces.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 5 isosceles right triangles (2 large, 1 medium, 2 small), 1 square, and 1 parallelogram.

questions.question_text: Can regular pentagons tile a 2D plane completely without gaps? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. Interior angle of regular pentagon is 108°. Since 360° is not divisible by 108° (3 × 108° = 324°), gaps remain at vertices.

questions.question_text: Explain which regular polygons can tile a plane by themselves (monohedral tessellation) and prove why using vertex angle sum.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Regular polygons tile if interior angle divides 360° completely: 1) Equilateral Triangle (60°): 6 × 60° = 360°. 2) Square (90°): 4 × 90° = 360°. 3) Regular Hexagon (120°): 3 × 120° = 360°. Only triangles, squares, and hexagons form monohedral regular tilings.

questions.question_text: A floor designer uses a square layout divided into a 7-piece Tangram set. (a) If area of square is 64 sq cm, find area of 7 pieces combined. (b) What fraction of area is formed by 2 large triangles? (c) Name all 4-sided shapes in Tangram.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Total area = 64 sq cm (tessellation preserves total area). (b) Two large triangles form 1/2 of total area = 32 sq cm. (c) The square and the parallelogram (two 4-sided shapes).
